requirement.title: Serve MCP over streamable HTTP with session semantics
requirement.body: Vision MUST expose MCP endpoints using the go-sdk StreamableHTTPHandler per server port. The server MUST support initialize, GET event streaming, and session teardown via DELETE while honoring Mcp-Session-Id semantics.

scenarios.title: Initialize returns a server session id
given: Vision daemon is running with a configured MCP server port
A client sends a valid initialize request
scenarios.when: The initialize request is handled by the streamable endpoint
then: Response is successful and includes Mcp-Session-Id
The session id can be used by follow-up requests

scenarios.title: Session teardown invalidates further use
given: A client has an active streamable session
The client sends DELETE for that session
scenarios.when: A later request reuses the deleted session id
then: The request is rejected as an unknown or expired session
No previous session resources remain attached

requirement.title: Enforce one subprocess per MCP session
requirement.body: Vision MUST maintain strict 1:1 mapping between each upstream MCP session and a supervised downstream subprocess. Session teardown or timeout MUST terminate only the owning subprocess and remove the mapping.

scenarios.title: Concurrent clients receive isolated subprocesses
given: Two clients connect concurrently to the same server port
scenarios.when: Each client performs tool calls and receives notifications
then: Each session maps to a different subprocess
Notifications and responses are routed to the correct session only

scenarios.title: Session timeout cleans up deterministicly
given: A session exceeds idle timeout or absolute TTL
then: The owned subprocess is terminated gracefully then forcefully if needed
The session mapping is removed and cannot be reused

requirement.title: Apply security and admission controls to all streamable endpoints
requirement.body: Vision MUST require bearer authentication, enforce a strict Origin allowlist, reject wildcard CORS, and enforce configured limits for max concurrent sessions, request sizes, and HTTP timeouts on streamable MCP endpoints.

scenarios.title: Unauthorized and disallowed origin requests are denied
given: A request is missing valid credentials or has a non-allowlisted Origin
scenarios.when: The request hits a streamable MCP endpoint
then: No session or subprocess is created

scenarios.title: Admission limits reject excess sessions
given: Configured max concurrent sessions is reached
then: The request is rejected with a clear limit error

requirement.title: Preserve operational compatibility and emit migration observability
requirement.body: Vision MUST preserve existing daemon command and health endpoint behavior while adding structured lifecycle/security logs for session creation, teardown, timeout, subprocess spawn/kill, and request denials.

scenarios.title: Daemon and health contracts remain stable
scenarios.when: Operators run daemon lifecycle commands and health checks

scenarios.title: Lifecycle and denial events are observable
given: Sessions are created, timed out, denied, and torn down during normal operation
then: Logs include session and server identifiers for lifecycle and denial events
Operators can correlate subprocess lifecycle with session lifecycle

wisdom.content: For foundation dependency pinning, `go mod tidy` removes go-sdk if it is not imported yet. Use `go mod edit -require=github.com/modelcontextprotocol/go-sdk@v1.0.0` (and download/build) to keep the dependency pinned before migration code lands.

go-sdk has NO StdioClientTransport type. Use `mcp.CommandTransport{Command: cmd}` instead. `Client.Connect(ctx, transport, nil)` starts the process AND performs the full initialize handshake automatically. The returned `*ClientSession` is immediately usable for ListTools/CallTool.

CommandTransport.Close() (called via ClientSession.Close()) follows the MCP spec teardown sequence automatically: close stdin -> wait TerminateDuration -> SIGTERM -> wait -> SIGKILL. No need for manual process group management - the SDK handles it.

For per-session proxy: the `getServer` callback in `StreamableHTTPHandler` runs synchronously before `server.Connect()`. This means you can spawn a downstream subprocess, discover tools via `ListTools`, and register proxy `ToolHandler`s all inside `getServer` — the upstream client will see the complete tool list in the initialize response. Use `Server.AddTool(tool, handler)` with the raw `*Tool` from `ListTools` — the `InputSchema` (a `map[string]any`) passes the marshal/unmarshal check for `"type": "object"` automatically.

go-sdk v1.0.0 client transport for Streamable HTTP is `&mcp.StreamableClientTransport{Endpoint: url}` (struct literal), NOT a constructor function. The `Endpoint` field is the base URL; the transport handles `/mcp` path, session headers, and SSE reconnection automatically.

go-sdk v1.0.0 StreamableClientTransport uses the Endpoint URL AS-IS (no /mcp appended). When the server's mux mounts the handler at /mcp, clients must use Endpoint: "http://host:port/mcp". In httptest (handler at root), plain URL works. In production (mux-routed), /mcp path is required.

For security middleware on Streamable HTTP: CORS preflight (OPTIONS) must skip auth but still validate Origin. The middleware order should be: Origin check → CORS preflight response → Bearer auth → inner handler. Use variadic parameter on AddStreamable() to keep backward compatibility with existing callers that don't need security.

For vision_add catalog server auto-installation: convert catalog.Entry to config.ServerConfig, allocate port via Config.NextAvailablePort(), add to registry, persist to servers.yaml via config.Save(), then registry.Start() which fires EventServerStarted → daemon.setupProxyForServer() → StreamableHTTPHandler automatically created. The entire Streamable HTTP proxy setup is event-driven, no special wiring needed.

go-sdk v1.0.0 StreamableHTTPHandler requires the Accept header to contain both 'application/json' and 'text/event-stream' for POST requests. Raw HTTP test clients must set Accept: 'application/json, text/event-stream' or they receive 400 'Accept must contain both'. The SDK client (StreamableClientTransport) sets this automatically.

When logging map length outside a lock scope (e.g., `slog.Int("count", len(m.sessions))` after `m.mu.Unlock()`), the race detector catches it as a data race. Always capture `len(m.sessions)` into a local variable BEFORE releasing the lock, then use the local variable in the log call.
